decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to hold the target range for the federal funds rate steady at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.

changes.quote: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace.
changes.explanation: The Fed upgraded its view of economic growth from moderate to solid.

changes.quote: Job gains have slowed in recent months but remain strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.explanation: The Committee noted that hiring has cooled off somewhat while overall labor conditions stay healthy.

changes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: Instead of raising rates further, the Fed left borrowing costs unchanged at this meeting.

changes.quote: Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Patrick Harker; Philip N. Jefferson; Neel Kashkari; Adriana D. Kugler; Lorie K. Logan; and Christopher J. Waller.
changes.explanation: New member Adriana D. Kugler participated in the unanimous vote to hold rates.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 20.84% APR costs about $86.83 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.35% and moved -2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.12% would fall by about $4.05 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.7%, and employers added an average of 202k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.7% over the past year (August 2023); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +4 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.94%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.16% on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that policymakers will keep watching incoming economic reports to determine if any additional policy tightening is needed. Educational forecasts suggest a 73% probability of another hold at upcoming meetings.
